structuredContent.markdown: # Ruff ## First try **Illustrative example; not executed in this review.** [Install Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/installation/), then save this as `sample.py`: ```python import math print("Ready") ``` Run this in the directory containing the file. It checks for unused imports without changing the file or loading project configuration: ```sh ruff check --isolated --select F401 sample.py ``` Representative diagnostic excerpt, not captured output (formatting varies by version): ```text sample.py:1:8: F401 `math` imported but unused ``` The location identifies the import; `F401` identifies the unused-import rule. Remove that line and repeat the check. A clean result means this selected rule found no violation in this file. ## Use it on your project Follow the [Ruff tutorial](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/tutorial/) to configure rule selection, file exclusions, and the target Python version. Run `ruff check` for linting; `ruff format` only formats code. Start without automatic fixes so you can inspect the diagnostics. ## Fixes and limitations Ruff distinguishes safe and unsafe fixes. Review proposed changes and run your tests after applying them. Record the tool version, configuration, and preview setting for repeatable results. ## Alternatives and complements Follow the [Ruff and mypy recipe](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/python-checks/) to check one project with separate lint and type reports. Pair Ruff with [mypy](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/) or [Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pyright/) when you also need type checking. Consider [Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/bandit/) for a dedicated Python security-rule workflow. [Pylint](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pylint/) uses inference and supports plugins; Ruff provides built-in rule families. Their rules overlap but are not interchangeable. Before switching, compare the diagnostics and plugin requirements of your project. The [official comparison](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/faq/#how-does-ruffs-linter-compare-to-pylint) explains these differences. Use the [finding review workflow](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/reviewing-findings/) to investigate a diagnostic and verify a correction.
